question.problem:
Given that $f(x)=|x-4|+2,$ on which of the following intervals is $f(x)$ invertible?

I. $x\in (-\infty ,3)$

II. $x\in (1,\infty )$

III. $x\in (-\infty ,5]$
question.worked_solution:
The graph of the function $f(x)=|x-4|+2$ can be obtained in the following way:

1\. Take the curve $y=|x|.$

2\. Translate it by $4$ units to the right,  to get $y=|x-4|.$

3\. Finally, translate $y=|x-4|$ by $2$ units up to get $f(x)=|x-4|+2.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196632/assets/56956d0f23ae6828098507712fd00525dc4f114a195716dc16e63d8475e9c143.png)

A function is invertible on a particular interval if and only if it's a one-to-one function on that interval. To determine the intervals on which the function is invertible, we use the horizontal line test. 

- The function $f(x)$ is invertible on the interval $x\in (-\infty ,3).$  Indeed, on this interval, any horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196632/assets/deb229df9f445a87215ff7c8fbb796113990df0c15124d5a6a01e199480620a4.png)

   

- The function $f(x)$ is not invertible on any of the intervals $x\in (1,\infty )$  and $(-\infty ,5].$ On each of these intervals, some horizontal lines will intersect the curve more than once.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196632/assets/eec9da919298bc8576580a0c7461e89625e1f4dbb49b9a5081dc959ca99153df.png)

   

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only".
